title: FDA's concerns with unapproved GLP-1 drugs used for weight loss
journal: US Food and Drug Administration, Postmarket Drug Safety Information for Patients and Providers, content current as of 4 February 2026
result: Compounded GLP-1 drugs are not FDA approved and are not reviewed for safety, effectiveness or quality before marketing. FDA received multiple adverse event reports, some requiring hospitalisation, possibly related to dosing errors with compounded injectable semaglutide, from patients measuring and self-administering incorrect doses and from health professionals miscalculating doses, and reports of doses, frequencies or titration beyond the approved label. As of 31 July 2025 FDA had received 605 adverse event reports for compounded semaglutide and 545 for compounded tirzepatide; state-licensed pharmacies that are not outsourcing facilities are not required to report adverse events, so under-reporting is likely. Other concerns: products arriving warm, fraudulent labels naming non-existent or uninvolved pharmacies, semaglutide sodium and semaglutide acetate salt forms that differ from the approved active ingredient, counterfeit Ozempic marketed in the US, illegal online sales that may contain wrong, harmful, too little or too much active ingredient, and products falsely labelled for research purposes. An import alert (66-80) targets GLP-1 active pharmaceutical ingredients with potential quality concerns.
